title: Run OpenVINS on EuRoC
subtitle: From a stereo image sequence and IMU measurements to a saved trajectory.
status: Upstream-documented guide; not executed or benchmarked here
summary: This guide follows the official OpenVINS EuRoC tutorial, from installing the estimator to saving and evaluating a trajectory. Run these commands in the documented Linux environment.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 20.04 with ROS 1 Noetic desktop-full installed using the upstream ROS1 installation instructions. Desktop-full supplies ROS tools and RViz; use Bash terminals. This is the upstream tutorial environment, not a native macOS workflow.

Git, a C++ build toolchain, CMake, catkin_tools, Eigen, Boost, Ceres, OpenCV with contrib modules, and the ROS dependencies listed below. Include the Python 3 packages for the evaluation plots used in step 6.
The EuRoC V1_01_easy ROS1 bag, downloaded from the official dataset source and saved as ~/datasets/euroc/V1_01_easy.bag.

steps.title: 1. Prepare the environment
steps.body: First install ROS 1 Noetic desktop-full on Ubuntu 20.04 using the linked upstream ROS1 instructions. After that, the commands below install the build and plotting dependencies used by this guide. OpenVINS package manifests also require cv_bridge, image_transport, and cmake_modules; they are included explicitly. Do not continue until installation succeeds.
steps.code:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install git build-essential cmake \
  python3-catkin-tools python3-osrf-pycommon \
  libeigen3-dev libboost-all-dev libceres-dev \
  libopencv-dev libopencv-contrib-dev \
  ros-noetic-cv-bridge ros-noetic-image-transport ros-noetic-cmake-modules \
  python3-dev python3-matplotlib python3-numpy python3-psutil python3-tk
source /opt/ros/noetic/setup.bash

steps.title: 2. Build the public upstream project
steps.body: Start in a Bash terminal with ROS sourced. Use a new workspace, then build all OpenVINS packages, including ov_eval. Continue only after catkin reports a successful build. Record the actual cloned commit with the experiment; the source revision shown on this page records the version reviewed for this guide.
steps.code:
source /opt/ros/noetic/setup.bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/workspace/catkin_ws_ov/src"
cd "$HOME/workspace/catkin_ws_ov/src"
git clone https://github.com/rpng/open_vins/
cd ..
catkin build
source devel/setup.bash
git -C src/open_vins rev-parse HEAD

steps.title: 3. Download and inspect the dataset
steps.body: Create ~/datasets/euroc if necessary, then download the V1_01_easy ROS1 bag through the official links and save it as ~/datasets/euroc/V1_01_easy.bag. Run the inspection command after the download completes. This remains an explicit manual download step; the commands below do not fetch the large dataset. The bag contains stereo images and IMU measurements.
steps.expected: Image topics /cam0/image_raw and /cam1/image_raw, plus /imu0, should be present.

steps.title: 4. Select the EuRoC calibration
steps.body: config:=euroc_mav selects the supplied estimator settings, IMU noise/topic file, and camera–IMU calibration. This run explicitly uses two cameras with stereo tracking. For your own sensor, these files must be replaced with its calibration and topic names.

steps.title: 5. Launch, visualize, and play
steps.body: Use four separate Bash terminals; each block sources its own environment and does not inherit variables or a working directory from another terminal. Start the estimator and RViz before playing the bag. Trajectory saving is enabled. The upstream recorder replaces an existing estimate.txt at launch, so choose a new filename when preserving repeated runs.

terminals.label: Terminal 2 · Estimator + trajectory recorder
terminals.code:
source /opt/ros/noetic/setup.bash
source "$HOME/workspace/catkin_ws_ov/devel/setup.bash"
mkdir -p "$HOME/vioverse-runs/openvins-euroc"
roslaunch ov_msckf subscribe.launch config:=euroc_mav max_cameras:=2 use_stereo:=true dosave:=true path_est:="$HOME/vioverse-runs/openvins-euroc/estimate.txt"

steps.expected: After initialization, RViz should show feature tracks and an estimated trajectory. estimate.txt records the current IMU pose estimates. A saved file alone does not establish a successful full run.

steps.title: 6. Inspect and evaluate the trajectory
steps.body: After playback finishes and the estimator completes processing, press Ctrl+C in Terminal 2 to close the estimator and recorder. Open a Bash terminal and run the block below. The ground-truth file is included in the public OpenVINS checkout, so no separate GT download or format conversion is needed. For V1_01_easy, upstream documents its recomputed IMU ground truth because of orientation errors in the original release.
steps.code:
source /opt/ros/noetic/setup.bash
source "$HOME/workspace/catkin_ws_ov/devel/setup.bash"
rosrun ov_eval error_singlerun posyaw "$HOME/workspace/catkin_ws_ov/src/open_vins/ov_data/euroc_mav/V1_01_easy.txt" "$HOME/vioverse-runs/openvins-euroc/estimate.txt"
steps.expected: The evaluator reports trajectory error statistics and matched samples. Check the timestamp span and evaluated overlap before interpreting an average.
steps.format: Trajectory text begins with time(s), px, py, pz, qx, qy, qz, qw; covariance entries may follow. In the reviewed ROS recorder, position is the IMU origin expressed in the global frame, and xyzw represents the IMU-to-global Hamilton rotation. These coefficients numerically match the internal global-to-IMU JPL quaternion; do not conjugate the exported file again. Published pose timestamps already use the IMU clock; do not add the camera–IMU offset a second time.
steps.alignment: posyaw aligns translation and yaw; record this choice with the result. Do not mix alignment modes when comparing systems.

links.label: Reviewed ROS pose direction and timestamps

checks.action: Confirm catkin build succeeded and source the workspace devel/setup.bash in that terminal.
Check the bag path, image and IMU topics, selected calibration, and initialization messages. Start the estimator before replaying the bag.
Confirm dosave:=true and that the output directory exists; the default launch does not save a trajectory.
Check seconds versus nanoseconds, quaternion order, pose frame, and ground-truth source. Use the supplied OpenVINS ground truth for this exercise.

nextSteps: Record the source commit, configuration, bag identity, camera mode, machine, launch command, output span, and alignment setting with the run.
Repeat with a single camera only after the stereo route works; use max_cameras:=1 and preserve the changed settings with the result.
Follow the calibration tutorial before using your own sensor.
localRunBoundary: This guide launches OpenVINS on your local machine. The commands were reviewed against upstream source; they have not been executed in this website build.
